Trends in Newly Diagnosed Diabetes For Everyone Nov. 17, 2026 Key points Initial findings on CDC surveillance data from 2024 and 2025 determine the most recent rate of new diabetes diagnoses, known as diabetes incidence. Data show age-adjusted diabetes incidence increased significantly from 2020 through 2025 after decreasing for more than a decade. Incidence refers to the number of people newly diagnosed with a condition over a certain timeframe. Surveillance results New CDC surveillance data show age-adjusted diabetes incidence increased significantly from 2020 through 2025 after decreasing for more than a decade. In 2020, the rate of diabetes incidence was 5.0 per 1,000 adults, continuing a decreasing trend from 2008 when incidence was 8.4 per 1,000 adults. New data show that diabetes incidence was 6.5 per 1,000 adults in 2024 and 7.1 per 1,000 adults in 2025. Figure. pages.text: Trove of Nazi Artifacts Found Stashed in Wall of German House Skip to main content Finds ranged from a portrait of Adolf Hitler to a revolver, gas masks, Nazi Party badges, brass knuckles, letters and documents. Ralf Blank / Hagener Stadtgeschichte Last month, a history teacher cleaning his aunt’s house in Hagen, Germany, after severe flooding discovered a trove of Nazi artifacts hidden behind a wall, reports David Crossland for the London Times . “I got goosebumps,” Sebastian Yurtseven told local media, as quoted by the Times . “I didn’t think it would turn into such a huge discovery.” When Yurtseven pulled out a rotten piece of plasterboard, he spotted a foot-wide space behind the wall containing a newspaper dated to 1945, writes Insider ’s Sophia Ankel. Investigating further, he found a cache of World War II–era artifacts, including a portrait of Adolf Hitler, a revolver, gas masks, Nazi Party badges, brass knuckles, letters and documents. Jeffrey Collins/AP hide caption toggle caption i Jeffrey Collins/AP South Carolina lawmakers dealt President Trump's national redistricting effort a blow Tuesday when the state Senate voted against redistricting there after three weeks of rushed hearings and long debate. Trump had been pushing state Republicans to redraw voting lines so they could flip a seat currently held by Democratic Rep. Jim Clyburn. It would have made all the state's seven congressional districts lean Republican and it would have extended the GOP lead in the national redistricting race, already netting them around nine more seats in the U.S. House. Early voting in the June 9 primary had started Tuesday morning and was one factor some Republican senators cited for opposing the redistricting, which had dragged on through weeks of on-and-off debate. TSCA Section 21 Under TSCA section 21, any person may petition EPA to initiate a proceeding for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule or order under: Section 4 -- rules or orders requiring chemical testing; Section 6 -- rules imposing regulatory controls on chemicals; Section 8 -- rules requiring information; or Section 5(e) or (f) -- orders affecting new chemical substances. The petition must be filed in EPA's Office of the Administrator and set forth the facts that are claimed to establish the necessity for the action requested. EPA is required to grant or deny the petition within 90 days from the day the petition is filed with EPA. If EPA grants the petition, EPA must promptly commence an appropriate proceeding. If EPA denies the petition, the reasons for denial must be published in the Federal Register. Обозначение обособленной велосипедной дорожки: highway=cycleway - основной тег линии, который указывает, что путь предназначен для движения на велосипедах. foot=no - явно запрещает движение пешеходов (если пешеходам запрещено находиться на этой дорожке). Если пешеходы разрешены, но дорожка разделена на зоны, используют foot=yes и segregated=yes/no . Велосипедная дорожка + тротуар: Комбинация тэгов для обозначения пешеходного тротуара, совмещённого с выделенной велосипедной дорожкой, которая конструктивно или визуально отделена от пешеходной зоны: highway=footway - обозначает, что данный объект является обустроенной дорожкой, предназначенной в первую очередь для пешеходов. footway=sidewalk - уточняет тип пешеходной дорожки. Этот тег указывает, что дорожка является тротуаром, то есть идет параллельно автомобильной дороге (обычно повторяя её геометрию). bicycle=designated - указывает на официальный юридический статус для велосипедистов. Это значит, что дорожка специально выделена/предназначена для движения на велосипеде (например, установлен соответствующий знак или нанесена разметка), а не просто «разрешена для транзита». segregated=yes - означает, что потоки пешеходов и велосипедистов разделены. We experience it at every moment. And refining our ability to measure it has had immense impact on our world. Surveyors measure local gravity every time they go out in the field. The scientific field of geodesy, which maps the Earth’s shape and predicts where water will flow and minerals can be found, is built on a foundation of gravity measurements. Accurate measurements of gravity are also key to how the world defines the kilogram, the fundamental unit of mass. Today’s most accurate gravity sensors use lasers and atomic clocks to measure how fast a macroscopic reflective object falls in vacuum. But scientists believe that a gravimeter based on the quantum properties of atoms could advance the frontier of precision and accuracy, potentially opening up new and powerful applications. Dakota (instead called Lakota by speakers of that dialect ) is the indigenous language of the Oc̣eṭi Ṡakowiƞ (Seven Council Fires) people of North America, consisting of the Bdewaḳaƞṭuƞwaƞ, Waḣpeḳute, Waḣpeṭuƞwaƞ, Sisiṭuƞwaƞ, Ihaƞkṭuƞwaƞ, Ihaƞkṭuƞwaƞna and Ṭiṭuƞwaƞ communities. Most members of these communities will describe themselves as Dakota (or Lakota for the Ṭiṭuƞwaƞ) people. Dakota and Lakota communities can be found in Minnesota, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Montana, Manitoba and Saskatchewan. All of these places have a rich geography of names devised by Oc̣eṭi Ṡakowiƞ people in the Dakota/Lakota language, including rivers, lakes, towns, islands, hills and more. People have traveled since the dawn of human history and some areas once had Dakota/Lakota communities that presently do not, and so other areas (such as Wisconsin, Iowa, Wyoming and Ontario) also have locations with names in the language. Historically, there have been far, far more Dakota and Lakota place names than those that survive for us to learn about them in the present. When assigning Dakota and Lakota names to map elements, I am mainly drawing on the (often lifelong) work of others; very few of my changes are based on personal local knowledge. I have focused on sources who are either directly part of, or at least worked closely with, authentic Oc̣eti Ṡakowiƞ communities. This is the language of nations that are alive today, and they have things to say! My major sources include: My mapping work owes an enormous amount to (and sits in the shadow of) the absolutely incredible Maḳoc̣e Waṡte map by Lakota historian Dakota Wind Goodhouse, who drew on a vast range of sources to populate the names of thousands of places. His blog The First Scout is one of the best public history projects you’ll find anywhere, and you should check it out. Sometimes my research has led me to different conclusions on the precise meaning and pronunciation of some place names, and the largest limitation of his map is the one he tells you about right away (it is a Landscape Map and so rarely discusses towns and cities) but this is still the single largest, most thorough map of Lakota/Dakota place names you will find anywhere until such time as I can somehow map twice as much content as I have. Last updated on 17 November 2026. My mapping on OpenStreetMap includes names in both Dakota and Lakota, with ISO codes dak and lkt respectively. This is an unusual approach compared to a lot of other multilingual mapping, so it’s worth explaining in more detail. Dakota and Lakota are two different dialects of the same language (and are two possible names for that language). They are mutually intelligible, and a fluent speaker of one can understand a fluent speaker of the other without difficulty. An analogy might be made to the Spanish spoken in Mexico vs the Spanish spoken in Spain - a speaker of the other dialect will seem to have a strong accent, unusual pronunciation, and some different word choices, but they are still clearly speaking your language . Both dialects are endangered, but there are substantially more Lakota speakers than Dakota speakers and this has been true for a long time. Dakota and Lakota share the vast majority of their vocabulary. Most words that differ between these dialects differ in predictable, formulaic ways that do not represent any difference in meaning (e.g. Oṭuƞwe vs Otȟúŋwahe or Bde vs Ble). The most meaningful differences in Lakota vs Dakota speech emerge in conversational flow, which rarely matters for place names. Close Tuwewanzi's Diary Dakota/Lakota Writing Systems and Orthography Posted by Tuwewanzi on 12 November 2026 in English . The Dakota/Lakota language has been a written language for only the most recent chapters of its history. Writing systems for the language were first devised by 19th-century missionaries who sought to promote literacy as a part of encouraging Dakota people to convert to Christianity. These missionaries, especially Stephen Riggs , developed an alphabet based on the Latin Alphabet to represent the sounds present in the language. All widely used methods for writing the language today are based on Riggs’ system with some degree of variation. There is no single writing system accepted by the vast majority of speaker communities. A variety of systems - or orthographies - exist with varying degrees of popularity, and invididual speakers and teachers often have strong preferences one way or another. Areas of debate include: May an orthography make use of special characters (ŋ, ǧ, ḳ, ú) or should writing be done only with characters that can be written with a standard English keyboard? The language contains vowels (a, i, u) that may be nasalized or not, depending on context; should the orthography note the difference? The language contains consonants (z, c, p, t, k, s) that may be aspirated for a harder sound or unaspirated; should the orthography note the difference? pages.description: Long thought to have been looted from northern England by Scottish tribes, the larger-than-life leg may have actually been displayed in Roman Scotland, before it was carefully dismantled and buried by retreating forces
pages.text: Two Centuries After This Bronze Leg Emerged From a Scottish Bog, Archaeologists Believe It May Have Belonged to a Towering Statue of a Roman Emperor on Horseback Skip to main content Curator Fraser Hunter examines the bronze leg. Duncan McGlynn In 1820, a larger-than-life gilded bronze lower leg was pulled out of a bog in the Scottish Borders region. For more than two centuries, historians discredited the idea that the Roman-era artifact came from Scotland, instead assuming that it was hacked off a monument in England and hauled north by marauding tribes. But ahead of “ Roman Scotland: Life on the Edge of Empire ,” an exhibition at the National Museum of Scotland (NMS), researchers have determined that the so-called “Milsington leg” was not stolen from the south, nor was it violently severed. Instead, they posit that it formed part of a colossal equestrian statue of the Roman Emperor Antoninus Pius that once stood in southern Scotland in the second century C.E., before it was dismantled by retreating Roman troops. “This really turns on its head our understanding of Rome’s second attempt at conquering Scotland,” Fraser Hunter , principal curator of prehistoric and Roman archaeology at NMS, says in a statement . The bronze leg shows no signs of being violently hacked off the larger statue. pages.description: Australian Jai Opetaia withdraws from his heavyweight fight with Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury's bout with Anthony Joshua in December.
pages.text: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Jai Opetaia pulls out of Deontay Wilder fight - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Deontay Wilder (left) has won 45 of his 50 fights, while Jai Opetaia has never lost By Kal Sajad BBC Sport boxing journalist Published 18 November 2026 Australian Jai Opetaia has withdrawn from his heavyweight fight with Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury's bout with Anthony Joshua. Unbeaten cruiserweight champion Jai Opetaia was set to step up to heavyweight for the first time to face American Wilder at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December. Opetaia, 31, did not give a reason for his withdrawal, but it is understood he aggravated a hand injury in training. "Apologies to everyone and especially [Wilder] and his team for withdrawing from the bout," he wrote on Instagram. "Fighter to fighter, I know the feeling and it's frustrating. I've always prided myself on fighting anyone, any place." Opetaia criticised "keyboard warriors" who suggested he was scared off by Wilder's powerful right hand. Opetaia, who has won all 31 of his professional bouts, reiterated his ambition to become undisputed cruiserweight champion. Unified champion David Benavidez has expressed an interest in facing Opetaia in 2027. Britons queuing up to fight Wilder Opetaia's withdrawal leaves a significant gap on the undercard of one of the biggest all-British heavyweight fights in history. It remains unclear whether former world champion Wilder, 41, will still feature on the bill, but several British heavyweights have expressed an interest in replacing Opetaia.
